entries.name: Mission Log 01: Drafted by Fate
entries.text: The message arrived the same way for each of you: a Stardust, Inc. tablet reading "You have been selected for mandatory service." One year of service, chosen at random from everyone in Stardust City. At least, that's what everyone kept saying, a little too cheerfully. You reported to the Training Facility in Sector 1, Lumina Core. A receptionist named Luca signed you in as Group E, and Major Yara Lenz led you up to Floor 45, R&D and Training. She explained the "All for One" initiative: a minimum of one year of paid service, with benefits for you and your families. After choosing weapons, each group was tested in the hologram room. Group E took down a pack of Zoloids, and Major Lenz noted that your synchronisation was the highest of the day. Then came the Bonding Ceremony. Each of you took a Bonding Crystal, and as it sank into your chest the world fell away into faint singing, and you met your Ethereal: • Hail found Melody sitting on the edge of a stage, next to the Ruby Flare, daring him to play. • Fallon stood on a bridge above the city with Aurelia, who asked which side she would save: the glowing districts or the slums. • Thalisteen was back in the forge of her childhood, where Kabesh greeted her: "Still making me wait, little sister?" • Silas woke in a silent gallery lined with his own sculptures, some he had made and some he hadn't yet. At the far end, Cassian was studying one of them: "You rushed this one." Before Silas could bristle, Cassian turned, genuinely pleased: "Finally. Someone worth talking to." When the light faded, Major Lenz had news: thanks to your performance, Group E was being placed in EIDOLON, Stardust's elite and secretive combat units.

entries.name: Mission Log 02: One Year Later
entries.text: Ten months on, EIDOLON Gamma had become one of the best squads in service, with few failures and strong bonds. People had started comparing you to SERAPH. Mission: monsters had got into one of the city's water treatment plants. You cleared out Zoloids and Giganticlaws that squeezed out of the pipework, swept the area, and replaced a damaged outflow grate. Your new handler, Thlaar, introduced himself over the radio (old Calton has retired) and called you "extremely expensive plumbers". On the way out, an Alarmbot stopped, scanned Hail, paused, then scuttled away. Back at HQ, Major Lenz had you fill in your paperwork, and you had the evening in the city. A few things felt off: • A soldier nearby muttered that he couldn't remember his past clearly. • Thalisteen felt a small spark sting where her crystal sits. • People were talking about a "rogue bonded pair". The next morning Thlaar called: the rogue pair had been reported near the slums, at a steel works on the edge of the Iron Pulse Ward. Command wanted them found and brought in for questioning.

entries.name: Mission Log 03: The Truth Bleeds Through
entries.text: Thalisteen started the morning at her forge, where her brother Karther was already at work. At the steel works, security robots held the perimeter. The same kind of Alarmbot scanned Hail again before running off, and a Charger bot sent you the floor plans. As you entered, your orders changed: eliminate on sight, no exceptions. The building was dark and wrecked. Floor by floor you fought off Selians and used crystal batteries to restore power and reach the warehouse. There you found the rogue pair: Felix, a Sen, and Mila, his Ethereal. They weren't hostile, just protective of each other. Mila started to call you "Stardust scum", then stopped as if she recognised something. Felix looked at Kabesh and asked: "Do you remember everything from before the bond?" Major Lenz came over the comms, demanding to know whether the pair had been eliminated. Then Felix and Mila began to collapse into each other, fusing into one screaming, crystal-covered form. It was a hard fight, but in the end you killed them, as Stardust wanted.

entries.name: Mission Log 04: Aftermath
entries.text: You were debriefed straight away, and it felt clinical. Did the rogue pair say anything unusual? Did your Ethereal show instability? Do you feel fully synchronised? Afterwards, your Ethereals weren't quite themselves. They hesitated more and asked strange, personal questions, like whether you remember your childhood clearly. That night at Silas's gallery, over drinks, a song by Hail's mum came on and Melody lit up: "Oh! I know this one!" Later, Thlaar called with a new assignment. Mission: support a containment facility in Narg for two or three days. ("I'd recommend the beach if you get a chance!") Medical Director Vrakkesh showed you round: wards full of bonded pairs who had been injured in the field or whose bonds were "breaking down". You worked the front desk, calmed confused patients and fixed a blown fuse during a power cut. You met three of the patients: • Nova Ember, restless, with sparks flickering round her hands. • Corvin, sharp-eyed and always watching. • Lumi Frost, who told Thalisteen she had admitted herself, and who looked at Kabesh and called him "Polaris". "That's not who you are." Near the end of a shift, the alarm went off: containment breach, Patient Room J. In the chaos, Unit SERAPH arrived, Stardust's elite bonded response team. They moved in perfect sync and resolved in seconds what would have been a full fight for you. You pushed them, and they gave you more than they meant to: • Commander Kael Vire: "You engaged before stabilisation protocols were complete." • Seris Vale: "Your bond efficiency is inconsistent." To Silas: "You're… not fully integrated yet, are you?" • Nyx-7 glitched mid-sentence at Thalisteen: "This configuration is… suboptimal… you were processed incorrectly." Then silence, as if nothing had happened. • Kael and his Ethereal spoke at the same moment: "Containment restored." Then: "You've completed your role. We'll handle the rest." • As they left: "Continue your development" to Hail, and "You were almost viable" to Fallon. When it was over, Nova and many other patients were dead. When you asked about Lumi, she wasn't on the patient list. The next morning your Ethereals were quiet. One by one they admitted they'd dreamt while you slept, and that it was the same dream for all of them, like a memory that wasn't theirs.

entries.name: Mission Log 05: Fault Lines
entries.text: After a mission, while you were still catching your breath, everything went quiet. Comms crackled, your Ethereals hesitated, and someone was simply there, as if they had been standing nearby the whole time. Not in uniform, not hostile. "You're further along than they expected." They spoke to your Ethereals as if they were people in their own right: "Do you hear them singing clearly yet?" With a small gesture your bonds twisted and slipped, then snapped back. "Still fragile." And then they were gone: "Next time… ask better questions." Comms snapped back with Stardust control demanding to know why your vitals had spiked. Nobody else had seen anything. In the parking garage, an armed squad was waiting: "EIDOLON Gamma. Come with us." The second debrief was nothing like the first. It was targeted and suspicious, and they wanted to know why the last few minutes of your data were missing. You all told the truth. During the questioning, Silas tried to run. He was killed. SERAPH were there too, watching. Seris said there had been interference; Stardust insisted there were no anomalies. You were held at HQ for 24 hours of monitoring, then released and taken off duty for a week. Happy Salazar was assigned to the squad. In the days that followed: • Your last mission log turned out to be incomplete, with about 30 seconds missing. • Your Ethereals began to crack. Aurelia remembered that she was once investigating something to do with Stardust, and Kabesh had flashes of medical equipment. • An anonymous text arrived: "They won't tell you what you saw. We will." • Stardust issued a directive: no unauthorised inquiry into recent anomalies. • Then a second message: "If you want answers, come now. They're moving the subjects."

entries.name: Mission Log 06: Dead Freight
entries.text: You wanted to follow the message, but going against Stardust's direct order made everyone nervous. Then Thlaar called on what sounded like a personal line, far too casually: "Not calling about anything! Just, uh… funny thing, the Sector 5 freight cams are down for a maintenance blackout from 6am to noon. Totally unrelated to anything." He hung up before anyone could ask. That settled it. The route led out through the ring of Crystal power generators, past the last of the slums, and onto open scrubland towards Sky Dock 7, a few kilometres outside the city. You reached a derelict pump station by the road just after dawn and stayed in cover, watching the main road. Hail caught a glint from the Sky Dock tower, and the glow coming from both of the convoy's vehicles. Thalisteen was the one who pointed out how lightly guarded it was: two armoured haulers, a handful of security robots, a Charger bot, an Alarmbot and a small human crew in Stardust grey. Before you could decide anything, an EMP cracked across the road and the lead hauler died. Camouflage tarps flipped back in the far ditch, and armed figures rose out of the dry grass. They had been lying there since before dawn. THORN. Happy was the only one to step out. He didn't take a side; he went to one of the human drivers to ask what was going on, and startled him. The driver shot him on reflex, and the Stardust robots marked Happy as an attacker. Hail tried to heal him from cover without being seen, and THORN spotted him. Hail stayed hidden, and when THORN's leader took a heavy hit, Hail chose to heal him too. When it was over, THORN didn't turn on you. Their leader, Rook, is a broad, heavily scarred Goith in faded Warrior-Monk robes under a patched armoured coat, carrying a polearm. Wick is a wiry Sen in a grey hooded jacket, with her scarf pulled low. They took you for travellers at first and talked mainly with Happy and Hail, until you showed them the text you'd received. Rook told you THORN had been sent the same message. The haulers were opened. Through the viewing windows were two containment pods: • One labelled MIRROR-01 — DUVALL, S. — STATUS: STABLE HOST. Inside, unconscious, was Silas. • One labelled MIRROR-01 — FROST, L. — STATUS: STABLE HOST. It was empty. You were still staring at the empty pod when one of the THORN guards called out: "This guy's moving!" Inside his pod, Silas's eyes had opened. His mouth was moving, but no sound came through the glass. That's not good.

entries.name: Dossier: Stardust, Inc.
entries.text: Status: Ruling power of Stardust City and most of Aethros Leadership: Stardust, Inc. Board of Directors History: The Stardust Empire won the last Great War with an army built around Crystal-powered robots, something the world had never seen. Most regions surrendered quickly. Nirmaan fought to the end and was defeated, and neutral Pustina was blockaded. Afterwards the empire lost interest in political rule and reformed as a corporation: Stardust, Inc. The war ended about ten years ago. In Stardust City: Stardust owns and runs everything, from food and sanitation to communications and construction. Every job in the city connects to it somehow. City laws come mostly from the corporate handbook, and image matters: vandalism and public disorder are punished harshly. Law enforcement: Robots patrol the streets. The Warrior-Monks officially oversee justice, but the Peacekeeping Division makes the real decisions. Its Charger robots are sent far and wide as scouts and enforcers. Stardust says the heavy robot presence is needed for as long as groups like THORN break the law. Mandatory service: Under the "All for One" initiative, citizens are selected at random for at least one year of paid service, with benefits for them and their families. What you've seen: • An order to eliminate a rogue bonded pair on sight. • A containment facility in Narg, full of bonded pairs whose bonds were "breaking down". • Your mission data with about 30 seconds missing, and an order forbidding any unauthorised inquiry into recent anomalies. • A lightly guarded convoy carrying containment pods out towards Sky Dock 7.

entries.name: Dossier: EIDOLON
entries.text: Status: Stardust, Inc.'s elite bonded combat units Street names: Possessed, Glow Dogs, Bonded To the public, EIDOLON are soldiers and peacekeepers who take on Stardust's most dangerous assignments. Most people know the name and little else: the units are surrounded by mystery, and membership isn't advertised. Every member is bonded to an Ethereal through a Bonding Crystal embedded in their body. How you joined: Group E was placed in EIDOLON straight after the Bonding Ceremony, after Major Lenz rated your synchronisation and bonding as exceptional.

entries.name: Dossier: EIDOLON Gamma
entries.text: Status: Active EIDOLON squad, currently off immediate duty and under observation Commanding officer: Major Yara Lenz Handler: Thlaar (took over from Calton, who retired) Members: • Hail Warick and Melody • Fallon Vega and Aurelia • Thalisteen and Kabesh • Happy Salazar, assigned after Silas's death • Silas Duvall and Cassian. Silas was killed during questioning. Record: About ten months of missions with very few failures. Other units have compared you to SERAPH. Notable missions: • Clearing monsters from a city water treatment plant. • The rogue pair at the steel works on the edge of the Iron Pulse Ward. • Support duty at the Narg containment facility, cut short by a containment breach.

entries.name: Dossier: Unit SERAPH
entries.text: Status: Stardust, Inc.'s elite bonded response team Public reputation: Called in when a situation is delicate, high-risk or politically sensitive. Known for a perfect mission record, and portrayed by the media as heroes. Members you've met: • Commander Kael Vire, with his Ethereal Lumen. Calm, precise, speaks as if the outcome is already decided. • Seris Vale, with her partner Ilan. Gentle but distant; she does most of the talking. • Dax Renn, with his Ethereal Pulse. Friendly, jokes in the middle of a fight. • Nyx-7. Inconsistent, and sometimes speaks like a system or an echo. What you've seen: • At Narg they arrived as the breach spiralled, moved in near-perfect sync, and resolved in seconds what would have been a full fight for you. • Some of them, with their Ethereals, speak the same words at the same moment. • They dismissed you: "You've completed your role. We'll handle the rest." • After the encounter outside the city, Seris told Stardust there had been interference. Stardust said there were no anomalies.

entries.name: Dossier: THORN
entries.text: Status: Outlawed group operating against Stardust, Inc. Presence: Significant, including inside Stardust City itself Stardust treats THORN as lawbreakers and uses them to justify the robots on every street. THORN fight Stardust where it is strongest: in the heart of its own city. What you've seen: THORN ambushed the convoy on the road to Sky Dock 7. They used an EMP and camouflage, and had been lying in the grass since before dawn. They were efficient, but not clean. They didn't attack you, and they had been sent the same anonymous message you were. Members you've met: • Rook: their leader. A broad, heavily scarred Goith in faded Warrior-Monk robes under a patched armoured coat, carrying a polearm. • Wick: a wiry Sen in a grey hooded jacket, with her scarf pulled low.

entries.name: Dossier: The Warrior-Monks
entries.text: Status: An ancient order, now mostly ceremonial For generations the Warrior-Monks protected Aethros from Monsters and dispensed justice. Stardust's robots have made them all but obsolete. The order still exists, and officially oversees justice in Stardust City, but its members are figureheads with no real say. Most people see them as a relic of an older age. Of note: Rook, THORN's leader, wears faded Warrior-Monk robes.
